Some mornings, as the first light of day stretches across the horizon, I find myself marveling at the economy of a single ray of sun. It carries warmth, color, possibility—everything we need to know that change is coming. In that moment, the world feels both infinitely large and intimately connected: a dewdrop on a blade of grass reflects the entire sky, and the breath of someone half a world away resonates in the same currents of air.

Stories do the same thing. A few words on a page can open doorways into memory, wonder, even heartbreak. They remind us that every human being carries a universe inside, full of hopes, fears, and secret strengths. A novelist in Mumbai and a poet in Buenos Aires might never meet, but their pages can cross paths, each reader holding just enough of their own life’s experiences to fill in the spaces between the lines.

When I write, I imagine offering fragments of that shared universe to whoever cares to look. A mention of a rain-slicked street corner, the crooked smile of a stranger, the lingering taste of mint tea—each detail is a vessel for memory. The more specific the image, the more freely anyone can apply it to their own story. That’s the paradox of creativity: the tighter the focus, the wider the embrace.

And so, as sunlight spills into the room, I let my thoughts wander where they will. I explore the edges of what I know, find delight in strange new questions, and trust that the simple act of recording a passing feeling might someday become a small gift to another reader’s dawn.
